title: Book 7 — Polymnia, Chapter 225
paragraphs: Two brothers of Xerxes, then, fell here fighting. Meanwhile a great struggle arose between the Persians and the Lacedaemonians over the body of Leonidas, until the Greeks by sheer valor dragged it away from the enemy and put their opponents to flight four times. This fight continued until the men who had come with Epialtes arrived; and when the Greeks learned that these had come up, from that moment the character of the combat changed. They drew back to the narrow part of the road, passed beyond the wall, and took up position together on the hillock — all in one body — except for the Thebans. This hillock stands at the entrance, where the stone lion now stands as a memorial to Leonidas. Here, defending themselves with daggers (those who still had them), and with their hands, and with their teeth, they were overwhelmed by the missiles of the barbarians — some of whom had pursued them directly and had torn down the fence of the wall, while others had come around and surrounded them on every side.
